title: Be, have, do: the helpers
goal: Use am/is/are, has/have and do/does correctly
intro: Three verbs do most of the work in English: be, have and do. They are main verbs (“I am tired”, “I have a car”, “I do yoga”) and also helping verbs that build questions, negatives and tenses. Getting their forms right fixes a huge number of mistakes at once.

rules.rule: be: I am, you/we/they are, he/she/it is.
do: I/you/we/they do, he/she/it does. Use it for questions and negatives in the simple present.

mistakes.why: After does, the verb goes back to the base form.

ex.q: We ___ at the airport when you called.
My boss don't like long emails.
ex.fixed: My boss doesn't like long emails.

ex.q: ___ you have any brothers or sisters?

ex.a: He doesn't have much time today.

ex.q: Make it negative: “She has a laptop.”
a: She does not have a laptop

talk: Describe a friend or family member: what they have, what they do and don’t do every day, and where they are right now.
